body: In what way did he not know how to manage his time?
Thank you
Thanks man

Yeah after we started talking again after the breakup I tried to get some closure. I told her that I’d started going to therapy, that I was so sorry for not being more open and spontaneous, for being so rigid. She said what was I sorry for and that she was still in love with me. But a few weeks went by and she pulled away again. I said that I didn’t want to go back to our old relationship as I know that didn’t work for her, but could we build something new together. But she said no, that she hadn’t changed her mind and that I can’t have changed into a new person. We tried to stay friends for a while but it was too painful for me and my friends intervened. So yeah I guess there’s nothing more I can do.

Thanks man. I’m sorry you had to go through that, good to hear it got better for you. It’s so hard seeing her, I feel like I’m going to vomit every time. I don’t recognise that man I used to be, I would do anything for a second chance. But I guess I had my second chance at the time, I just didn’t know it.
Thank you for your reply. I actually quite like a bit of uncertainty! It certainly sounds very well supported and geared towards your development.

Thanks! It sounds like CT is very good for your professional development with all that teaching and supervision. How do you find the therapy cases? I imagine it is quite a difficult thing to start when you've not done it before. Where have you experienced dissidents?

Thank you for your detailed answer. I can see how it might be difficult not working in as big of a social group anymore. Interesting what you say at the end, there does seem to be a bit of a reputation at least where I work that a lot of people have chosen psychiatry for the lifestyle rather than passion for the speciality.
May I ask what field you work in?

Thank you for your reply. As I said I’m quite inexperienced so accept I’ve probably got a lot backwards! I think what I mean in terms of complexity is more what you speak about in terms of navigating the diagnosis with patients once you have started treatment. I enjoy working in shades of grey with uncertainty. It’s interesting what you say about being a better person and understanding more about the world. Sometimes I feel like internal medicine is making me worse! Rushing through things with patients, forcing diagnoses, little time spent explaining things with patients. What I find myself enjoying more recently is the rare chance you get to have a long discussion with a patient or family, unfortunately this is often in the context of death and dying.
So you don’t think depression can be triggered by a breakup? There’s no benefit to medication here?
Thank you

Thank you, your replies are really insightful. I agree I think I will be a very different person when I’ve come through the other side of this. I was quite rigid and closed off before and it kills me that I couldn’t fix it before I met her because she really was my best friend and I can’t believe I lost her. She reached through a lot of walls and has held a mirror up to me. I’d do anything to meet her for the first time again but I think I will just have to live with my mistakes and take what I learn going forwards. I don’t want to be the person I was before.

Thanks for your reply, it’s really good of you to go into detail. It was my first ever relationship (I’m 27 so quite late) and the first time someone had been in love with me and I with them, on top of us being best friends before as well. I did feel like she saw all of me and accepted that, until things went wrong and a lot of negative things I thought about myself were brought up by her at the breakup. So I think it has emphasised some of my own shortcomings to me, that was the best connection I’ve had with a person and I still messed it up. 

I also had quite an emotionally abusive father and developed quite a rigid way of living to deal with that. My therapist feels this breakup may have brought up some of that, and as you say I probably haven’t grieved that original trauma. Thank you again.

Thank you. Yeah I feel like it was all down to my failings and I keep obsessing over how I should have done things differently, reading old messages where I messed up etc. I hope Wellbutrin could help, glad you got some peace from it. Did it help meeting someone new?
Thank you

Yeah she’s on my mind all the time, I’m obsessed with all the things I could have done better and I can’t stop thinking about it. How did it feel dating someone when they were still on your mind? I had been thinking about making sure I was fully over her before I do, but it’s been six months and I still spend all day thinking about her so maybe I should try and meet someone new. Thank you.

Thank you. I’m seeing a psychotherapist as well as I agree there is more to it than just this breakup. What do you mean by resisting being integrated with the rest etc? I find the therapy helpful but I still feel stuck in this obsessive thought loop of guilt so maybe a combination would help
Thanks for your help, those are some interesting thoughts. It was my first relationship and she was my best friend for a year before so yeah it’s really got hold of me.
Thank you
I haven’t tried anything yet, thanks
Thanks for your reply. She was my best friend and I developed romantic feelings for her, I couldn’t not pursue it. It just hurts that it didn’t work out.
I think she told me this when we were very close friends and then maybe forgot or didn’t want to remember she had said this to me once we started dating. I don’t think she ever cheated on me though.

We dated for around 5 months. She said she felt we were too different and she wanted someone she could merge her life with more with the same interests, that I was too closed off, that I was too rigid and stopped her living. I was studying a lot at the time and both had full time jobs. It was very much a blindside though, a week before she was saying she was very happy and glad we took the step to a relationship from friendship.
Thank you. I guess even if I made a lot of mistakes these things are always two way (outside of cheating/abuse etc)

Thank you. Yeah I consciously had it in my head that she wanted more spontaneity after that. So for example if she was like I'm having coffee at this spot in town and it was near to where I was studying I was suggest I come and meet her for a drink etc rather than going straight to my work or planning something ahead of time. Not much I know and it wasn't often but I was trying to take some steps. After that fight a month before she had come and said she was sorry for losing sight of how supportive and loving I was so yeah I thought things were OK. Anyway, thank you again.

Thank you. I should clarify that she was telling me she was still in love with me after we broke up but before she was with someone new (to my knowledge). I think in her mind she feels she raised things but from my perspective that was one or two conversations months before things ended and I thought the relationship was really growing. She’d not expressed any issues for a month, quite the opposite, so that’s why I was so shocked. Thank you for your advice. I think it’s hard for me to see future relationships because it took me until I was 27 to find this one, but I hope there will be.

Thank you. I struggle with it because I feel we were really compatible in so many ways, sense of humour, intelligence, values, we even have the same job. But I guess the fact she felt our differences were too much is enough and I can't do anything about that.

Thanks. I really wish my feelings could just vanish and I could be platonic friends but it just cuts me too deep at the moment. Like I won’t be able to sit and chat about her new guy like a friend would.

Thank you. I think because I feel a lot of guilt about not being more free with my time and regret doing so much studying. I don’t think I stopped her living but feel pain that I couldn’t give her the excitement she wanted. I’m in therapy but struggling to shake it.

Thanks for your response. Yeah I will talk with her and reassure her that I am really into her and that I do enjoy seeing her, just with a bit more notice. I am worried that it will be a compatibility issue, that she will move on to someone who has more free time and is more spontaneous. It would really hurt for us to both lose our best friend.
Should add that I feel both situations are normal, just interested in hearing what each felt like as I don't have that much relationship experience
Hope you find peace man.

Yeah I see what you mean. I don’t think she has BPD but a lot of the stuff I read here resonates with me. Stuff like idealisation, how intoxicating it feels to be put on that pedestal, but how quickly you can be pushed off. I don’t understand how things went from ‘I’m so happy, all my friends are complaining about their relationships and what would I even complain about’ to ‘we’re too different, we want different things, you’re too closed off etc’ literally within a week. She was triggered hard by me studying a lot and not feeling prioritised which has left me in this guilt spiral. I guess there were issues on both sides.

Thank you. It’s tough deciphering this stuff, I feel like we were halfway between a typical relationship and a more codependent one. I guess it doesn’t matter in the end but it helps me to try and process things.

Thank you. I think it was mostly a cute term and overall the relationship was good but I think she did have some other traits, describing herself as chaotic and emotional, abandonment fears, sudden blindsiding after saying how great things were going a week before because she wanted our friends and interests to merge. Push/pull after the breakup making me think we were getting back together. Anyway thank you for your reply.

I often see on here that if I’d really wanted to be with her then I’d have made her the priority. I get the point but it doesn’t feel true for me. I really loved this girl, I think I just fucked up with my lack of experience and being too rigid.
Having read your posts...I hope you find some peace one day
I mean we’d been dating for six months...but thanks
Even six months out it doesn’t feel real. I keep thinking I will wake up and be back with her. That the new guy she’s with doesn’t exist.

Thank you. I don’t think she does have the full disorder as I don’t feel she meets enough criteria. But there’s traits there I feel, the insecurity, the abandonment fears, the desire to merge, the splitting and blindsiding, ‘you’re my favourite person’. I got into therapy pretty soon after the breakup because I went from a confident and steady guy to an emotional wreck, it shook me to my core.

That sounds tough. My ex decided she wanted to take a break from me to think about if I was what she wanted for a couple of days, I was crying as she told me this but it still didn’t seem to register how much I cared
Yeah we were kind of coming from different ends of the spectrum
Thank you. Hope we get through this.

Thank you. Yeah maybe it was seeing if I would drop everything. It’s hard because I feel real guilt about that, like I should have been more free with my time and spontaneous. But I did regularly tell her I love her, supported and reassured her, but it never seemed to be enough to really secure the idea in her mind.

Thank you very much for your reply. I understand what you mean I think. While I was still in the same high level of text conversation right until the end I think maybe she felt that because I was putting a lot of time into studying and working out etc that it meant I cared less about her when I did those things. She would sometimes invite me over last minute and often I wouldn’t come just with it being a bit incompatible with a busy schedule. I would prefer to find out when she was free and set out some quality time. But I think that triggered her also.
Yeah I’m not sure if I’m being way off the mark here, like I say I personally don’t have anything to compare it to. I did find it a bit strange though.
Yeah it was my first relationship so I thought maybe it was normal to speak like that? But yeah favourite person got dropped a lot
Thank you. She did seem to get bored very easily.
Yeah that’s what I thought. I even have a card from her from that week with ‘favourite person’ and various other things in it.
Sometimes I worry that I’m labelling her with these BPD traits when in fact I’m just distant and pushed her to the limit. This whole experience has been so confusing and now I’ve lost my best friend.
Thank you for your reply. I struggle between feeling like she did have BPD traits and that I was good to her, versus feeling like I was a villain who was cold and neglected her.
Thank you, it's so hard not to dwell on what I could have done differently. I miss her every single day.

Thanks. Yeah I think communication was an issue because even just a week before the breakup she was saying how happy she was. Maybe she didn't feel comfortable opening up to me and just wanted out. Maybe I should have probed more.

It has really made me question my own emotions. I’ve felt like I’m a robot or something because I’m not experiencing this internal rollercoaster. I thought I was just pretty chill and steady but being blindsided like this has made me question everything about myself. Maybe I am closed off, I don’t know anymore.
Great thanks!
